title: Auserene vs Stoic: one connected journal or a routine toolkit?
seoTitle: Auserene vs Stoic (2026): AI journal, meditation, streaks, price
description: Auserene vs Stoic, from Stoic's own pages (Nov 2026): connected features, meditation from your day, memory you can edit, streaks, Apple Watch, price.
dek: Stoic gives you routines, a meditation library and streaks side by side. Auserene connects your notes, an evening conversation, a meditation from your day, memory you can read, your people and your habit goals.
titleOptions: Auserene vs Stoic: one connected journal or a routine toolkit?
Stoic vs Auserene: meditation, streaks and AI memory compared
Auserene or Stoic? An honest comparison from one of them
Is the Stoic app worth it? How it compares with Auserene

faq.a: If you want one journal that does it all, yes. Auserene connects quick notes, an evening conversation that writes your entry, a meditation made from your day, memory you can edit, people and habit goals. Stoic is the better pick for a big breathing and meditation library, streaks, or Mac, Android and the web.
Yes, guided and unguided meditation plus 20+ breathing exercises. They're a library, the same for everyone. Auserene writes a new guided meditation from each day's conversation.

Stoic has a free plan with daily prompts, quotes, basic guided journals and a limited set of breathing and meditation exercises. Its App Store listing shows several paid prices without billing periods, plus a $299 lifetime option. Auserene has a free plan with no time limit, and Premium is $11.99 a month or $105.99 a year.

faq.q: Does the Stoic app use AI, and which provider?
faq.a: Yes, in its Premium + AI tier. Stoic's help center says AI entries go to OpenAI and may be kept up to 30 days, not for training, while its privacy policy names OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini. The AI that reads your Auserene journal works under zero-data-retention terms and keeps nothing after a reply.
Yes, under Premium, and you can turn them off. Auserene has no streaks. Its habit goals have a 21, 42 or 64-day finish line and never mark a missed day red.

Yes, plus a web app, though its help center says the Android app has fewer features and can't sync with iOS yet. Auserene is on iPhone and iPad with an Apple Watch app today, and Android and web versions are in the works.

informationGain: A disclosed head-to-head built only from Stoic's own pages on November 19, 2026, including its App Store prices that carry no billing periods, the mismatch between its help center (OpenAI, current entry only) and privacy policy (OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini, historical journals) on AI, and its device-and-iCloud storage model, set against Auserene's meditation written from your day, readable memory and no streaks.
